title: Historic First: Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade Postponed to Saturday Due to Severe Storms
snippet: For the first time in its 100-year history, the iconic Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been postponed due to extreme weather, pushing the holiday tradition to Saturday as crews race against the clock.
content:
In an unprecedented turn of events, New York City's most iconic holiday tradition will not take place on Thanksgiving morning. For the first time in its 100-year history, the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been officially postponed due to severe weather threatening the Tri-State area.

Organizers announced Wednesday afternoon that the milestone 100th parade will now step off on Saturday, Nov. 28, at 8:30 a.m. ET. Broadcast coverage will remain on NBC and Peacock, with a Spanish-language simulcast on Telemundo.

Dangerous Weather Forces Last-Minute Delay

The decision comes as a powerful storm system approaches the East Coast, bringing predictions of torrential rain, localized coastal flooding, and potentially hazardous wind gusts. The National Weather Service issued a high-wind warning starting Thursday morning, raising serious safety concerns for the parade's legendary giant helium balloons. New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill declared a state of emergency on Wednesday in anticipation of the storm's impact.

"The safety of our participants and spectators is our top priority, and after close consultation with our City and agency partners, we have made the decision to move this year's celebration," Macy's said in an official statement.

Strict guidelines established in 1998 dictate that the giant balloons must be grounded if sustained winds exceed 23 mph or gusts top 34 mph. Those regulations were put in place following a 1997 incident where a wind-whipped "Cat in the Hat" balloon crashed into a lamppost, severely injuring a spectator. While balloons were grounded entirely due to bad weather in 1971, the event itself had never been rescheduled until now.

Scrambling Logistics and Shuffled Lineups

The delay leaves production crews and city agencies working on a hyper-compressed schedule to reconfigure logistics, security, and street closures that normally take weeks of careful planning. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani acknowledged the disruption while urging patience from residents and tourists alike.

"I know that this change of plans will cause inconveniences, yet safety has to come first," Mamdani said. "On Saturday, when balloons climb into the sky, every New Yorker and everyone visiting will be able to take in a show that is both truly spectacular and also safe."

While Macy's executive producer Will Coss expressed optimism about preserving the original lineup, the schedule shift has inevitably disrupted travel plans for some acts. The University of Alabama announced that its Million Dollar Band will have to miss the rescheduled parade to travel back home for a scheduled football game. However, several marquee acts, including the Broadway casts of Wicked, Hamilton, and The Rocky Horror Show, are still slated to perform on Saturday morning.
